facility_roles.locator: arXiv:2606.29381, Sec. II (KamLAND Detector and Dataset)
facility_roles.note: The KamLAND collaboration places the detector at Mt. Ikenoyama in Kamioka; the Atlas records that Kamioka mine complex as facility:kamioka-observatory. No page consulted names the Kamioka Observatory as the host of KamLAND (the official KamLAND site's technical pages returned 404 on every URL tried, checked 2026-09-17), so the host link is an inference and stays uncertain.
facility_roles.quote: The KamLAND detector was located 1000 m underground at Mt. Ikenoyama in Kamioka, Japan.

intervals.label: first results data-taking period
intervals.note: Start is January 2002 at month precision: arXiv:hep-ex/0405074 (Motoki et al., Tohoku Research Center for Neutrino Science) says 'In January 22, 2002, KamLAND started the data-taking', while the KamLAND proceedings arXiv:hep-ex/0405001 (Hatakeyama, for the KamLAND Collaboration) says KamLAND 'started operation on January 21st 2002', so the day is not fixed here. The 2026 collaboration paper (arXiv:2606.29381, v2 of 21 Oct 2026) says "KamLAND began data taking in March 2002 and ended data taking in August 2024.", and the first-results exposure began on 4 March 2002 (arXiv:hep-ex/0212021); this record does not resolve the January/March difference. The end (2024-08-27) comes from the KamLAND collaboration paper quoted above; the TAUP 2025 slides give the day: "Last physics run on August 27th 2024".
intervals.quote: In January 22, 2002, KamLAND started the data-taking.

intervals.label: first-results exposure used in the 2002 discovery paper
intervals.note: The paper reports a 145.1-day exposure but no explicit calendar bounds were seen verbatim in the fetched abstract.

end.note: Q-EYES 2025 slide: "Installation of new PMTs starting in autumn 2026 / Filling with LS starting in summer 2027 / Restart of DAQ in spring 2028"; TAUP 2025 slide: "KamLAND2 dismantling & constrution ongoing -> expected launch in 2028!".

intervals.label: KamLAND2 upgrade: detector dismantling and rebuilding (no data taking)
intervals.note: Day from the TAUP 2025 slide "Last physics run on August 27th 2024 -> dismantling of detector ongoing"; month confirmed by the collaboration paper. The restart date is a plan from December 2025 and the slide chain ends with "KamLAND2-Zen will start in FY2028-2029??" (question marks on the slide).

quantity.note: The KamLAND collaboration states 1 kton of liquid scintillator in the inner detector (a nominal, rounded figure, hence ~1000 t).
quantity.quote: The ID contained 1 kton of LS enclosed in a 13-m-diameter nylon/EVOH (ethylene-vinyl alcohol copolymer) balloon, which was supported by non-scintillating buffer oil.

website.note: Homepage only; the 'About KamLAND' technical sub-page returned 404 on every URL tried (checked 2026-09-17).

name: KamLAND
notes: KamLAND's later physics program (solar neutrinos, geoneutrinos, and the separate KamLAND-Zen double-beta-decay search using the same detector:kamland) is not detailed here beyond the `secondary_kinds` tag; KamLAND-Zen has its own record (experiment:kamland-zen), which references detector:kamland.

physics_goals.quote: a search for the oscillation of ν̄e ’s emitted from distant power reactors. The long baseline, typically 180 km, enables KamLAND to address the oscillation solution of the ‘solar neutrino problem’ using reactor anti-neutrinos
physics_goals.value: Measure the flux and energy spectrum of electron antineutrinos from distant nuclear reactors to test neutrino oscillation solutions to the solar neutrino problem

summary.plain: A huge detector in a Japanese mine that watches antineutrinos from nuclear power plants across the country, and in 2002 gave the first direct proof that they disappear the way solar-neutrino theories predicted.
summary.technical: Reactor-antineutrino oscillation experiment in the old Kamiokande cavity of the Kamioka mine, using a ~1000 t liquid-scintillator detector to observe a flux-weighted average of many distant Japanese reactors; started data-taking in January 2002 and reported first results (evidence for reactor antineutrino disappearance) later that year.

unique_capabilities.locator: arXiv:hep-ex/0212021 (Phys. Rev. Lett. 90, 021802), opening paragraph and Fig. 4 caption
unique_capabilities.quote: The long baseline, typically 180 km, enables KamLAND to address the oscillation solution of the ‘solar neutrino problem’ ... The solid dot is the KamLAND point plotted at a flux-weighted average distance (the dot size is indicative of the spread in reactor distances).
unique_capabilities.value: A single very large liquid-scintillator detector far from many reactors, seeing a flux-weighted average baseline rather than one fixed near/far pair
